newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian state-run bank to lay off 2,000 staff.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian state-run bank to lay off 2,000 staff.

text.p: Tanzania's biggest bank, the state-owned National Bank of Commerce (NBC), will lay off 2,000 more employees in a drastic move to improve performance, a senior bank official said on Wednesday.
Ngalimecha Ngahyoma, spokesman for the loss-making bank, told Reuters the cuts, to be implemented by the end of September, would bring to just over 2,000 the total number of staff in full employment.
A retrenchment programme which started three years ago has seen the current workforce reduced to around 4,000.

The bank was founded in 1967 by former president Julius Nyerere and operated as a monopoly under his socialist command economy. It then had 205 branches across the east African country with about 9,800 staff but now has only 130 branches.
The planned cuts follow a detailed review of the bank's operations at branches and head office and take into account forthcoming changes to NBC's organisational structure.

The bank is due for privatisation later this year as part of economic reforms backed by Western financial institutions. But the plan has proved to be a thorny political issue for President Benjamin Mkapa following Nyerere's involvement.
Nyerere, who still wields strong influence over the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi party, has been critical about credit provisions for the rural community once the bank is privatised.
But his detractors counter that the bank is too impoverished to offer credit and is a national embarrassment.

Parliamentary legislation needed for NBC's privatisation is expected to be passed this month. Irritated at the slow pace of NBC's privatisation, the World Bank has put on hold payment of a Structual Adjustment Credit (SAC) worth $125 million.
Ngahyoma said current planning was for 87 branches to operate as micro-finance facilities and 37 for trade and regional finance.
